facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s with a history of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
The lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
A well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque, 15 × 12 cm, was seen over the right side of the anterior chest wall around her operation scar
Scattered within the erythema were multiple palpable small nodules
Negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
Right mastectomy scar with a large well-defined area of erythema and multiple, scattered small nodules
Nearly complete remission of skin lesions after treatment

concepts.why: The presence of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, a well-demarcated warm erythematous plaque, and multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels are characteristic of inflammatory breast cancer.

The history of right breast cancer and the presence of a lesion at the operation site with multiple nodules and carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels suggest a locoregional recurrence of breast cancer.
The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels and a history of breast cancer suggest cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer.
The negative results for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 suggest triple-negative breast cancer.

rationales.F01: History of breast cancer increases the likelihood of locoregional recurrence or cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F02: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules is suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer or cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F04: Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque with multiple palpable small nodules is highly suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer.
rationales.F06: Negative ER, PR, and HER2 status is characteristic of triple-negative breast cancer.
rationales.F07: Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels is diagnostic of cutaneous metastasis or inflammatory breast cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels and a history of breast cancer supports cutaneous metastasis, while the clinical presentation could also suggest inflammatory breast cancer, but the specific finding of carcinoma cells in lymphatic vessels leans towards metastasis.
